academic.passage: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy, primarily in the form of glucose. This process occurs mainly in the chloroplasts of plant cells, where chlorophyll captures sunlight. The significance of photosynthesis extends beyond individual plants; it is crucial for sustaining life on Earth by providing oxygen and serving as the base of the food chain. Without photosynthesis, most life forms would not survive, as it is the primary means of producing organic matter from inorganic substances.
